detail.abstract:
In this study, we suggest that crowding-out effects are unlikely when incentivizing behaviors that we refer to as mixed-motive—that is, behaviors motivated by both self-interest and prosociality. Vaccination is the prominent example we analyze: people vaccinate both to protect their own health and to contribute to herd immunity by protecting others.

Building on signaling theory, we assume that people derive utility from signaling their prosociality. Incentives can crowd out prosocial motivation when they block the opportunity to send a clear prosocial signal, as in purely prosocial behaviors like charitable giving. Mixed-motive behaviors differ: they never allow for a clean prosocial signal in the first place, because self-interest is always a plausible motive. As such, providing financial incentives does not further constrain signaling opportunities, and we therefore predicted no crowding-out effects to emerge when incentivizing mixed-motive behaviors. Our experimental study supports this prediction.

title: Bilingual/Localization Strategies in Latin American Expansion: Four Cases

detail.title: Bilingual/Localization Strategies in Latin American Expansion: Four Cases
detail.abstract: In Latin America, language proficiency is a critical business imperative, not a courtesy. Companies that neglect Spanish-language capability experience significant market failures, while those pursuing comprehensive localization capture cross-border demand and achieve sustainable growth.  This study examines four multinational corporations to demonstrate how language strategy directly influences market performance. Golden Dragon, a Chinese manufacturer, encountered substantial operational challenges in Mexico due to linguistic isolation. Best Buy's Spanish-language e-commerce platform generated substantial engagement and revenue gains. Uber Eats' literal translation approach in Colombia undermined user adoption, whereas Netflix's investment in Spanish and Portuguese content and localized interfaces drove rapid subscriber expansion.  Drawing on industry reports and case studies from September 2017 to September 2025, supplemented by foundational examples, our findings reveal that strategic localization functions as competitive infrastructure. Organizations that proactively address linguistic needs, employ professional translation, develop bilingual teams, and deliver culturally equivalent experiences achieve superior operational, financial, and reputational outcomes. Conversely, inadequate localization correlates with misunderstandings, poor adoption, and diminished revenue.  While language alone does not determine success, strategic attention to localization provides organizations with both protective and growth-oriented advantages in Latin American expansion.

title: From Vibe-Coding to Vibe-Governance: How AI Is Rewriting the Rules of Power
affiliations: Better Regulation Delivery Office — BRDO

detail.title: From Vibe-Coding to Vibe-Governance: How AI Is Rewriting the Rules of Power
detail.abstract: This paper introduces and coins the conceptual framework of Vibe-Governance-how conversational AI restructures access and power in public policy. Just as "vibe-coding" made software creation accessible through natural-language interfaces, Vibe-Governance applies the same translation layer to policymaking, lobbying, advocacy, and justice. I define related terms-Vibe-Policymaking, Vibe-Lobbying, Vibe-Advocacy, and Vibe-Justice-and ground them in Ukraine-based pilots: AI-assisted court-decision analysis, legislative monitoring, EU directive alignment, and policy alerts. The central claim is dual: (1) conversational interfaces widen participation and compress policy cycles by making institutions explainable and editable in plain language; (2) without guardrails, they risk widening equity gaps, amplifying bias, and weakening deliberation. I propose practical oversight principles-traceability logs, human-in-the-loop review, inclusion budgets, option-set generation, and impact audits-to govern AI-enabled governance. The contribution is a clear vocabulary, a practice-grounded framework, and an agenda for building governance at thought speed without sacrificing legitimacy.

title: Corporate Social Responsibility and Consumer Purchase Intention: The Mediating Role of Brand Equity — A Systematic Review (2018–2025)
affiliations: Bahauddin Zakariya University and Bahauddin Zakariya University

detail.title: Corporate Social Responsibility and Consumer Purchase Intention: The Mediating Role of Brand Equity — A Systematic Review (2018–2025)
detail.abstract: This study systematically reviews research published between 2018 and 2025 to examine how Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) influences consumer purchase intention through the mediating role of brand equity. Drawing on 28 empirical and conceptual studies sourced from Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, Google Scholar, and SSRN, the review applies a thematic synthesis approach integrating cognitive, affective, and contextual perspectives. Findings reveal that CSR enhances consumer purchase intention primarily by strengthening brand image and brand equity, with authenticity, brand-CSR fit, and cultural context serving as critical boundary conditions. Authentic and value-driven CSR initiatives foster consumer trust, emotional attachment, and moral legitimacy-key components of brand equity that drive favorable purchase decisions. Conversely, perceived opportunism or greenwashing weakens these effects and may erode brand capital. The review highlights persistent methodological homogeneity, overreliance on cross-sectional surveys, and limited exploration of digital CSR communication. The study contributes a conceptual framework clarifying the CSR-brandbehavior mechanism and proposes a future research agenda emphasizing longitudinal, experimental, and cross-cultural designs. The findings offer strategic insights for marketers seeking to align ethical responsibility with brand value creation and consumer loyalty.

title: AI-Driven Leapfrogging in Higher Education: A Strategic Framework for Equity, Innovation, and Academic Transformation

detail.title: AI-Driven Leapfrogging in Higher Education: A Strategic Framework for Equity, Innovation, and Academic Transformation
detail.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming higher education by enabling personalized learning, streamlining administrative tasks, and enhancing global access to academic resources. This paper investigates how AI-driven technological leapfrogging allows institutions-particularly in underresourced regions-to bypass conventional development phases by directly adopting advanced AI systems. Using a mixed-methods approach, including case studies from Rwanda, India, and the UAE, this study explores how AI fosters equity, increases faculty efficiency, and enhances student engagement. The findings indicate that AI-integrated learning systems significantly improve academic outcomes, with 78% of students reporting performance gains and 85% of faculty citing improved efficiency. However, challenges persist, including data privacy concerns, algorithmic bias, and unequal access to AI tools. The study emphasizes the need for ethical AI frameworks and inclusive policies to ensure sustainable integration. By framing AI as both a catalyst for innovation and a tool for equitable academic advancement, this research contributes to the discourse on educational technology and policy reform in global higher education.

publicationDetails.detailsText: University of Chicago, Becker Friedman Institute for Economics Working Paper No. 2025-135

detail.abstract: Research shows responsive caregiving enhances children's brain development, with parental knowledge predicting positive behaviors and outcomes. However, knowledge varies widely across educational levels, highlighting the need for targeted interventions. Despite evidence that this knowledge can be improved, no comprehensive metric exists for efficient assessment. We introduce SPEAK (Survey of Parent/Provider Expectations and Knowledge), a computeradaptive tool grounded in item-response theory that we created, to address this gap by measuring parental and educator knowledge across development domains with precision and speed. This paper details SPEAK's development, including domain construction, cognitive interviewing, expert review, psychometric calibration, and validity evidence. SPEAK offers a flexible, scalable solution for clinical, educational, research, and policy settings. By identifying knowledge gaps, it enables tailored interventions, supports professional development, and informs policy, ultimately improving parent-child interactions and child outcomes. Our tool bridges critical gaps in assessing child development knowledge, advancing research and crosssector collaboration to promote early childhood development worldwide.

title: Optimal Collateral Collection for Clearing Interbank Payments
affiliations: , University of Toronto - Rotman School of Management, University of Toronto - Rotman School of Management and Hefei University of Technology

detail.title: Optimal Collateral Collection for Clearing Interbank Payments
detail.abstract: Efficiently clearing daily payment obligations is critical for financial stability. Central banks manage this process by requiring commercial banks to post collateral, creating a system-wide trade-off between the opportunity cost of pledged assets and the borrowing costs incurred during collateral shortfalls. We first model this problem from a central planner's perspective as a twostage stochastic program. We solve this model to obtain a closed-form, newsvendor-like solution for the optimal total collateral that minimizes the system's expected costs. We then analyze the problem as a cooperative game to explore the potential for further cost reductions through collaboration among banks. A key contribution is the design of a practical mechanism that ensures the stability of the grand coalition. Going beyond standard concepts like the core, we argue that such allocations are insufficient as they only guarantee stability ex-ante; they can become unstable once daily payment obligations are realized and ex-post costs deviate from expectations. Our mechanism therefore specifies rules for internal borrowing and lending and introduces a novel algorithm for allocating collateral requirements, ensuring a fair and stable distribution of realized costs. We validate our framework using a unique dataset of interbank payments from Payments Canada, demonstrating the efficacy of our proposed mechanisms and quantifying substantial potential cost savings.

title: Valuing Questions when Answers are Cheap: A Dynamic Framework for the Economics of Curiosity in the AI Era
affiliations: Independent Research

detail.title: Valuing Questions when Answers are Cheap: A Dynamic Framework for the Economics of Curiosity in the AI Era
detail.abstract: In an era increasingly defined by Artificial Intelligence (AI), the marginal cost of obtaining answers is rapidly approaching zero. This paradigm shift creates an economic paradox: as answers become abundant, the ability to formulate meaningful questions-a manifestation of curiosity-emerges as a critical and scarce resource. However, classical and neoclassical economic frameworks lack the tools to formally define, measure, and value curiosity as a productive asset. This paper seeks to fill this theoretical gap by proposing a foundational framework for "Curiosity Economics." We introduce the concept of "Curiosity Capital" as a distinct form of human capital. We then develop and compare two quantitative models for its measurement: a static model based on the Kullback-Leibler (KL) Divergence, and a novel dynamic model. We present this dynamic model in both its ideal continuous integral form and its practical discrete summation form. Through a detailed case study, we demonstrate the model's application and reveal a "path independence" property, which we argue exposes the core components of curiosity. This analysis leads to the proposal of a second-order model for future research. The paper concludes by discussing the profound implications of this framework for education policy, corporate innovation strategy, and the valuation of long-term scientific research.

title: Optimal Parking Planning for Shared Autonomous Vehicles: A Two-Stage Stochastic Programming Approach

detail.title: Optimal Parking Planning for Shared Autonomous Vehicles: A Two-Stage Stochastic Programming Approach
detail.abstract: The successful deployment of shared autonomous vehicle systems relies on well-designed parking lots, which serve as both storage depots and dispatch hubs. A key challenge is the coordination between parking planning and fleet operations, exacerbated by varying land prices and demand uncertainty. To address these issues, we develop a two-stage stochastic programming model. The first stage determines the parking lot location, capacity, and initial SAV allocation, considering land prices. The second stage optimizes fleet operations through a time-space network to track vehicle movements. The model is solved using the sample average approximation method and validated through a case study in Chengdu, China. Results demonstrate that our approach consistently outperforms benchmark methods, highlighting the importance of an optimizationbased decision support for SAV parking planning. Further analysis reveals that as the fleet size increases, parking lots increasingly function as intermediate stops during operation, substantially reducing unnecessary vehicle movements and associated energy consumption.

title: Economic Development in the 21st Century
affiliations: George Washington University

detail.title: Economic Development in the 21st Century

publicationDetails.journalName: IZA Institute of Labor Economics Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract: The goal of economic development is to raise standards of living in LDCs, to be achieved by accumulating both human and non-human capital so as to maximize production net of the cost of these investments. An LDC economy is modelled with two sectors, modern and traditional, each of which uses its own type of human and non-human capital in production. Sector-specific human capital is specified as an attribute embodied in its workers, who have agency to choose their sector of employment and level of education. Earnings of labor are the sum of two components: recovery of human capital investment costs (e.g., student loan repayments) and an economic rent (i.e., profit) available for current consumption. The consumption-maximizing resource allocation equalizes rates of return to investments in all types of capital and allocates workers between the two sectors so that labor rents (i.e. consumption levels) are the same in both. Policy implications emphasize removing economic, social and cultural barriers to economic mobility for all resources.

title: Social Learning among Urban Manufacturing Firms: Energy-Efficient Motors in Bangladesh

detail.title: Social Learning among Urban Manufacturing Firms: Energy-Efficient Motors in Bangladesh

publicationDetails.journalName: IZA Institute of Labor Economics Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract: Knowledge spillovers among firms are widely viewed as a key driver of agglomeration and growth, but are difficult to estimate cleanly. We randomly allocated an energy-efficient motor  a servo' motor  among leather-goods firms in Dhaka, Bangladesh, and tracked adoption, information flows, beliefs about energy savings, and other variables. We use the difference between actual exposure and expected exposure (from simulated randomization draws) to identify the effect of exposure. We find a robust positive effect of exposure to treated neighbors within a small geographic area (500 meters in our baseline specification) on information flows and adoption. A marginal value of public funds (MVPF) calculation taking learning spillovers into account yields a significantly larger value than one considering only treated firms and suggests that adoption subsidies would be a cost-effective policy intervention.

title: Performance Pay and Happiness: Work vs. Home?
affiliations: University of Trier, University of Wisconsin at Milwaukee and University of Trier - Faculty of Economics

detail.title: Performance Pay and Happiness: Work vs. Home?

publicationDetails.journalName: IZA Institute of Labor Economics Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract: Using German survey data, we show conflicting influences of performance pay on overall life satisfaction. The overall influence reflects a strong positive influence through domains of life satisfaction associated with the job (job satisfaction, individual earnings satisfaction and household earning satisfaction) and a strong negative influence through domains away from the job (health satisfaction, sleep satisfaction and family life satisfaction). This trade-off between work and home generalizes and helps explain many previous studies examining much more specific consequences of performance pay. Finally, controlling for the mediating role of the domains, the direct influence on life satisfaction is positive for women and insignificantly different from zero for men.

title: Worker Beliefs about Firm Training
affiliations: Technische Universität München (TUM), Ifo Institute and Ifo Institute

detail.title: Worker Beliefs about Firm Training

publicationDetails.journalName: IZA Institute of Labor Economics Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract: Firm training is key to meeting changing skill demands, yet little is known about the role of workers beliefs in shaping training participation. In a survey of 3,701 workers in Germany, we document that they expect substantial returns to firm training  both in terms of earnings and non-pecuniary outcomes such as promotion chances, job task complexity, or enjoyment. These beliefs predict actual and intended training participation. Lower-skilled workers anticipate smaller non-pecuniary returns, partly explaining their lower uptake. An information treatment addressing return beliefs significantly increases training intentions among lower-skilled workers, suggesting that targeting beliefs may help narrow participation gaps between lower- and higher-skilled workers.

title: Working from Home and Mental Health: Giving Employees a Choice Does Make a Difference
affiliations: University of Trier - Faculty of Economics and University of Brighton

detail.title: Working from Home and Mental Health: Giving Employees a Choice Does Make a Difference

publicationDetails.journalName: IZA Institute of Labor Economics Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract: Previous studies on working from home (WFH) and employee well-being have produced conflicting results. We hypothesize that giving workers a choice over whether to use WFH plays a crucial role in the consequences for well-being. This has a series of testable implications for empirical work. Using panel data from the UK, our fixed effects estimates show that not only the actual use, but also the pure availability of WFH is linked with improved job-related and overall mental health. Not controlling for the pure availability of WFH implies that the positive influence of the actual use of WFH is underestimated. However, we find a positive link between the use of WFH and overall mental health only for the years before and after the pandemic. The link was negative during the COVID-19 crisis where WFH was largely enforced. Moreover, gender moderates the influence of WFH on mental health. For women, both the actual use and the pure availability of WFH are positively associated job-related and overall mental health. For men, we find a more mixed pattern where either only the pure availability or only the actual use has an influence on mental health. Men are more likely to over- or underrate the consequences of WFH than women.

title: The Moderating Role of Job Autonomy in the Relationship between the Use of Performance Appraisals and Job Satisfaction
affiliations: IZA Institute of Labor Economics, RWTH Aachen University - School of Economics and Business Administration and RWTH Aachen University

detail.title: The Moderating Role of Job Autonomy in the Relationship between the Use of Performance Appraisals and Job Satisfaction

publicationDetails.journalName: IZA Institute of Labor Economics Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract: We explore the moderating role of job autonomy for the link between the use of performance appraisals and employees job satisfaction. Results based on German linked employer-employee panel data show that performance appraisals are linked to higher job satisfaction at moderate levels of job autonomy, whereas this positive relationship weakens at both low and high levels of autonomy. Moreover, the interplay between performance appraisals and job autonomy appears sensitive to broader institutional and contextual factors, such as the existence of employee representation, perceived job security, and design of the performance appraisals. Our findings highlight the complex role of job autonomy in shaping employee responses to performance management, underscoring the need for context-aware human resource practices.

title: The Second Spanish Immigration Boom
affiliations: Charles III University of Madrid

detail.title: The Second Spanish Immigration Boom

publicationDetails.journalName: IZA Institute of Labor Economics Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract: International migrants choose their country of residence to maximize their utility. As a result, their choices are informative about the relative attractiveness of countries. This paper explains why Spain became the fourth most attractive country in the world for international migrants in the period 2015-2024, what I define as the Second Spanish Immigration Boom of the century. First, an accounting decomposition shows how, contrary to other destinations, Spanish-specific factors, correlated with economic conditions and general migration policies, have a larger weight in explaining immigration to Spain than origin-specific factors. Second, the causal relevance of bilateral visa policies is also shown, particularly in the context of Latin American immigrants, by using origins that are required a visa to enter Spain as a control for visa-free access countries in a generalized differences-in-differences setting. Finally, the effects of the Boom on immigrant selection are also analyzed, finding that the Second Boom was different from the first because educational selection improved.

title: Deep Learning for Portfolio Optimization: An AI-Driven Approach to Risk-Adjusted Returns
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Deep Learning for Portfolio Optimization: An AI-Driven Approach to Risk-Adjusted Returns
detail.abstract: Portfolio optimization is one of the central problems in finance, concerned with allocating capital across assets to achieve the best possible balance between risk and return. Since the development of Modern Portfolio Theory (MPT) by Markowitz in the 1950s, financial researchers and practitioners have sought methods to enhance diversification and improve the stability of returns. However, classical frameworks suffer from restrictive assumptions such as normally distributed returns, constant correlations, and market stationarity. These assumptions often fail in real-world conditions, leading to portfolios that are suboptimal in volatile and complex market environments. The growing availability of financial data and advancements in computational methods have opened the door for artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning (DL) and deep reinforcement learning (DRL), to transform portfolio optimization. Unlike traditional econometric and machine learning models that primarily focus on return prediction, DL and DRL approaches offer the potential to directly optimize investor-relevant objectives such as the Sharpe ratio, Sortino ratio, or Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR). This shift in methodology aligns model training more closely with actual investment outcomes. Recent studies highlight this promise. Zhang, Zohren, and Roberts (2020) introduced a deep learning framework that directly maximizes the Sharpe ratio for exchange-traded fund (ETF) portfolios, bypassing the forecasting stage altogether and demonstrating superior performance during turbulent periods such as the COVID-19 pandemic. Similarly, Huang, Zhou, and Song (2024) developed a Sharpe-ratio-based Actor-Critic reinforcement learning framework capable of dynamically adjusting allocations in the CSI 300 Index, achieving stronger risk-adjusted returns than mean-variance optimization and risk parity benchmarks. Together, these works illustrate both the viability and advantages of risk-aware DL and DRL methods. This paper builds on these foundations by proposing a hybrid framework that combines multi-agent reinforcement learning with multi-objective optimization, targeting Sharpe, Sortino, and CVaR simultaneously. By integrating forecasting-driven features through recurrent and convolutional architectures with decision-making processes rooted in reinforcement learning, the proposed approach aims to deliver robust, adaptive, and risk-sensitive portfolio strategies. The study contributes to the growing literature on AI in finance by (1) expanding risk-adjusted objectives beyond single metrics, (2) leveraging multi-agent specialization for enhanced adaptability, and (3) systematically benchmarking performance against both classical and modern baselines.

title: Beyond the Clinic: How Short Video Platforms Influence Patients’ Online Medical Consultations
affiliations: Hefei University of Technology - School of Management, Hefei University of Technology, The School of Management, Hefei University of Technology and University of Florida - Warrington College of Business Administration

detail.title: Beyond the Clinic: How Short Video Platforms Influence Patients’ Online Medical Consultations
detail.abstract: Short video platforms have emerged as influential channels through which physicians both disseminate medical knowledge and share aspects of their personal lives. The implications of these behaviors for patients’ choices in online medical consultations represent a compelling issue for both practitioners and scholars. Drawing on social penetration theory, our empirical study demonstrates that physicians who engage in science popularization and personal self-disclosure on short video platforms attract a greater number of patients seeking online consultations. Importantly, the observed effect arises from physicians’ self-disclosure in both breadth and depth, mediated through two pathways: video content and presentation, and responsive communication in comments. Collectively, these findings enrich the theoretical understanding of physician-patient interactions in digital settings and offer practical guidance for integrating short video platforms into online healthcare strategies. In particular, they underscore how physicians can foster patient trust and deepen engagement by strategically leveraging short-form video content.

title: The Past and Future of U.S. Structural Change: Compositional Accounting and Forecasting
affiliations: Federal Reserve Banks - Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond, Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond and Princeton University - Princeton School of Public and International Affairs

detail.title: The Past and Future of U.S. Structural Change: Compositional Accounting and Forecasting

publicationDetails.detailsText: Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond Working Papers, volume 25, issue 08, 2025[10.21144/wp25-08]

publicationDetails.journalName: Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: We explore the evolving significance of different production sectors within the U.S. economy since World War II and provide methods for estimating and forecasting these shifts. Using a compositional accounting approach, we find that the well-documented transition from goods to services is primarily driven by two compositional changes: 1) the rise of Intellectual Property Products (IPP) as an input producer, replacing Durable Goods almost one-for-one in terms of input shares in virtually all sectors; and 2) a shift in consumer spending from Nondurable Goods to Services. A structural model replicating these shifts reveals that the rise of IPP at the expense of Durable Goods is largely explained by increases in the efficiency of IPP inputs used in production: input-biased technical change. Trend variations in sectoral total factor productivity, and their attendant effects on relative prices and income, are the main driver of evolving consumption patterns. Both reduced-form and structural forecasts project these trends to continue over the next two decades, albeit at lower rates, indicating a slower pace of structural change.

title: From Adversity to Tenacity: CEO Early-Life Disaster Experience and Corporate Resilience
affiliations: University of International Business and Economics (UIBE) - Business School and College of Finance and Statistics, Hunan University

detail.title: From Adversity to Tenacity: CEO Early-Life Disaster Experience and Corporate Resilience
detail.abstract: This study leverages granular establishment-level data to identify firms’ exposure to natural disasters and investigates how CEOs’ childhood experiences of natural disasters shape corporate resilience to such exogenous disaster shocks across the United States. At the establishment level, we find that establishments led by CEOs who experienced fatal disasters in early life exhibit higher sales, employment levels, and labor productivity in the aftermath of natural disaster shocks. Notably, this positive effect of CEOs’ traumatic early-life experiences is concentrated among male CEOs and younger CEOs. At the firm level, we aggregate the disaster exposure of each firm’s establishments and document a positive association between a CEO’s early-life exposure to fatal disasters and the firm’s financial and stock market performance post-disasters. This relationship is evidenced by superior operating performance, higher sales growth, and stronger stock performance. We attribute these findings to, and provide empirical evidence for, the observation that firms led by CEOs with fatal disaster experience adopt more conservative financial policies. This policy choice suggests an intentional strategy to accumulate slack resources, which in turn enhances firms’ resilience to future adversities. Collectively, our results indicate that traumatic events during the formative early-life period can leave enduring imprints on individuals’ psychosocial resilience. These imprints, in turn, improve CEOs’ cognitive and emotional capabilities when navigating analogous adverse situations in the context of firm management.

title: The Multi-Product Newsvendor Problem: Review, Extensions, and Directions for Future Research
affiliations: Johns Hopkins University - Carey Business School, China Europe International Business School (CEIBS), University of Florida - Warrington College of Business Administration, California State University, East Bay, University of Florida and University of Florida

detail.title: The Multi-Product Newsvendor Problem: Review, Extensions, and Directions for Future Research
detail.abstract: In this paper, we review the contributions to date for the multi-product newsvendor problem (MPNP). Our focus is on the current literature concerning the mathematical models and the solution methods for the multi-item newsvendor problems with single or multiple constraints, as well as the effects of substitute and complementary products on the stocking decisions and expected profits. We present some extensions to the current work for a stylized setting assuming two products and conclude with directions for future research.

detail.title: Research on a monorail hoist track safety operation and maintenance system based on visual perception and intelligent control
detail.abstract: The monorail hoist  track is a critical component of auxiliary transportation in coal mine shafts, and its safety condition directly impact transportation efficiency and safety. Due to prolonged exposure to frequent powerful impacts from monorail hoist locomotives, the track is prone to defects. Currently, inspections primarily rely on manual patrols, which suffer from high labor intensity, numerous interfering factors, low detection accuracy, and poor control effectiveness. There is an urgent need to improve both intelligent detection and control of track conditions. However, existing intelligent detection technologies, due to their complex algorithms and numerous model parameters, fail to meet the operational requirements  in terms of detection speed and accuracy, and the implementation of intelligent control remains challenging. Based on this, this paper proposes a solution combining visual perception and intelligent control. First, the visual detection algorithm is optimized by proposing a lightweight semantic segmentation method based on the DeepLabv3+ network. The lightweight MobileNetV2 network is used as the feature extraction network, with a coordinate attention mechanism embedded. Second, an intelligent control system is designed, comprehensively evaluating track deflection angles,leading to the development of a self-adaptive intelligent control system  for monorail hoists. Experimental results show that the improved detection algorithm significantly reduces the number of parameters in the segmentation model, improves computational speed, and maintains high segmentation accuracy. The intelligent control system effectively prevents track fractures caused by power imbalance, ensuring the continuous safety of coal mine transportation. This provides technical support for the efficient monitoring and intelligent maintenance of monorail tracks.

detail.title: Real-Time Tracking for Non-BS6 Chassis: Finding the Right Market Fit
detail.abstract: This research paper addresses the critical challenge of tracking non-BS6 drive-away chassis, vehicles that lack On-Board Diagnostics (OBD) ports, license plates, and other conventional identifiers. These chassis, often in transit from manufacturing facilities to export ports, pose significant tracking difficulties due to the absence of built-in electronic systems. The objective of this study is to identify the most reliable, cost-effective, and operationally feasible tracking solution for such vehicles. Using a non-probability purposive sampling method, over 40 companies offering tracking technologies were initially identified. In-depth discussions were conducted with a shortlisted set of providers based on technical compatibility and operational capacity. The study critically analyzed both hardware-based GPS/GSM solutions and mobile SIM-based tracking alternatives, evaluating each against key parameters such as real-time visibility, reverse logistics, ease of deployment, and cost. Among the companies evaluated, some emerged as top candidates, offering practical and scalable rental-based GPS tracking solutions that eliminate the need for capital investment while ensuring real-time monitoring. The research concludes that rental-based GPS/GSM systems present the most effective model for tracking non-BS6 chassis during transit, balancing technological reliability with economic viability.

detail.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive framework for transitioning from a Gross Domestic Product (GDP)-centric economic model to a National Bio-Ecologic Resource Score (NBERS)-driven Bio-Ecologic Economy. The NBERS is proposed as a holistic metric to measure prosperity through ecological health, social equity, and human well-being, addressing the limitations of GDP in accounting for environmental degradation and social disparities. Developed by the ERES Institute for New Age Cybernetics, this framework integrates novel biometric, cybernetic, and governance systems to foster long-term human and planetary flourishing. Key proprietary components, including Emotional Personal IQ Real and Quantum (EPIR-Q), Aura Resonance Index (ARI), Sovereign Universal Glycan Architecture for Resilience (SUGAR), EarnedPath (EP), Bio-Electric Signature Time (BEST), and FAVORS (Fingerprint, Aura, Voice, Retina, Signature), are introduced as foundational elements. These are supported by innovative governance models (CBGMODD, P³), adaptive learning systems (Empirical Realtime Education System - ERES EP, PlayNAC), and robust certification protocols (TETRA CERT). This revised draft aims to enhance clarity, provide more detailed explanations of these concepts, and outline a more practically grounded roadmap for implementation, emphasizing the shift from resource extraction to sustainable prosperity rooted in health, law, and protection.

title: Perceptions of Public Debt and Policy Expectations
affiliations: Johns Hopkins University, International Monetary Fund (IMF) and International Monetary Fund (IMF) - Fiscal Affairs Department

detail.title: Perceptions of Public Debt and Policy Expectations

publicationDetails.journalName: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Utilizing surveys of over 27,000 respondents from 13 advanced and emerging market economies, we explore how knowledge and beliefs about government debt influence expectations of tax and expenditure policy changes. Individuals systematically underestimate debt levels, especially in high-debt countries, and believe that the burden of fiscal adjustments will disproportionately affect them. Greater lifetime exposure to fiscal consolidation increases pessimism about future economic prospects, diminishes trust in government, and is associated with expectations of higher debt, future taxes increases and spending cuts, and inflation. Informing respondents about their country’s debt levels reduces expectations of tax increases in stable debt contexts and raises expectations of spending cuts in countries with rising debt with the influence of this information moderated by individuals’ past experiences with fiscal consolidation.

title: State Capacity, Institutions and Growth
affiliations: International Monetary Fund (IMF) and Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS)

detail.title: State Capacity, Institutions and Growth

publicationDetails.journalName: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Can simply exceeding a critical tax-to-GDP threshold bring about an accelerated trajectory of economic growth and development in a country? We conduct new event studies and exploit a richer dataset to revisit Gaspar, Jaramillo and Wingender’s 2016 “tax tipping point” result. Both with their regression discontinuity approach and a dynamic difference-in-differences estimation, we find that cumulative growth over 10 years increases by 10 percentage points when a country’s tax-to-GDP ratio increases above a 10 percent threshold. Further, we show that crossing the threshold coincides with the beginning of significant improvements in measures of a country’s financial development, government effectiveness, legal framework, and governance. Event studies additionally reveal that only transformational episodes of tax increases above the threshold deliver these gains: episodic crossings that fail to bring tax revenues durably above the threshold and that don't coincide with improvements in financial development and government effectiveness yield fleeting gains. Our results suggest that a minimal tax capacity is necessary for growth but emphasize that only a sustained tax increase associated with other developmental progress is sufficient.

detail.title: AI Projects in Financial Supervisory Authorities

publicationDetails.journalName: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper discusses the imperative for financial supervisory authorities to enhance their toolkit through the adoption of Artificial Intelligence in response to the growing digitalization of financial services. It aims to assist authorities in safely and effectively overseeing applications of Artificial Intelligence in the financial sector by proposing a tailored project management methodology for implementation of Artificial Intelligence by financial supervisory authorities that address unique risks and align initiatives with strategic goals. Key challenges, including ensuring explainability and mitigating bias, with a focus on stakeholder collaboration, are emphasized, alongside prerequisites for successful deployment, such as robust governance frameworks and adequate resources.
